title: Scheherazade, III, opening: Stokowski and Monteux
question: Why does the same violin melody sound different under Stokowski and under Monteux?
intro: Two violin sections begin the young lovers’ movement of Scheherazade, playing in G major above held lower strings. Stokowski’s Philadelphia players slide between notes and take the tune slowly. Monteux’s San Francisco orchestra takes it at a faster tempo, with a brisker pulse beneath the long phrases.

recordings.label: Leopold Stokowski, Philadelphia Orchestra
recordings.note: The strings play the melody in broad phrases, with audible slides between notes.

recordings.label: Pierre Monteux, San Francisco Symphony
recordings.note: Monteux keeps the tempo moving through the lovers’ music, under the long phrases in the violins.

passages.label: Opening melody, violins
passages.note: Both violin sections play the melody together. Long notes lead into short runs above held chords in the lower strings.

passages.label: Quick notes within the melody
passages.note: The violins play quick notes, then return to the longer notes of the melody. The lower strings continue their quiet accompaniment.

passages.label: Crescendo and diminuendo, violins
passages.note: The violin phrase becomes fuller and louder, then quietens as the melody continues.
